new_statements.quote: Nugunu has two phonemic tones, H and L. These may be realized at any number of phonetic pitch levels because of the process of downdrift, in which the pitch of any H tone following a L is lower than the pitch of preceding H tones. Rising, falling, and rising-falling contours are aiso found, formed by the juxtaposition of two or more dissimilar tones.

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record, no existing statement). The work supplies a tone-only classification (two-tone language, H/L, downdrift) and is silent on word stress; this matches what the already-held Boyd 2015 (sec. 2.5.5 p.115, two-tone system) and Orwig 1989 (DELAN p.288, one tonal opposition H vs L) say, none of which states anything about stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Nugunu is described as a tone language with two phonemic tones (H, L), downdrift, downstep of H after H-L-H spreading, and contour tones from juxtaposed level tones; tense/mood marked by tonal morphemes on the verb. The paper contains no statement about word stress, accent or prominence: a search of the whole scanned text for stress / accent / prominen finds only 'accents' in the sense of tone diacritics (orthography note, p.3). No stress placement can be drawn from it.
new_statements.secondary_stress: none mentioned (no stress discussed at all)
new_statements.exceptions: none regarding stress; tonal irregularities only (irregular verb classes, verbs with final falling vs level tone, sec. 2.3.4-2.3.6)
new_statements.identity_note: Nugunu (Gunu, 'Yambassa' in older usage), Bantu A.60 Sanaga/Mbam group, Central Province (Mbam department), Cameroon, ca. 30,000 speakers per the paper; the paper treats the verb phrase; no dialect is named in the introduction (Robinson's related SIL work is on North Gunu).
